subject.title: [Feature]: Deeplink/contentIntent support in system.notify for Android nodes

question: Should Android `system.notify` notification taps be allowed to launch external deeplinks, and if so should they share the same allowlisted policy as the broader Android URL-launch request?
rationale: The current code gap is clear, but choosing the allowed target model crosses a native Android app-launch boundary and cannot be safely inferred from source alone.

options.title: Share Allowlisted URL Policy
options.body: Implement notification tap targets only after defining the same explicit scheme/host allowlist and rejection semantics used for the broader Android URL-launch capability.

options.title: Restrict To OpenClaw Deep Links
options.body: Allow notification taps only for OpenClaw-owned app screens or actions, reducing launch risk but not satisfying arbitrary companion-app deeplinks.

options.title: Defer Tap Targets
options.body: Keep Android `system.notify` notifications non-actionable until maintainers decide the broader native deeplink/app-launch policy.

recommendation.title: Share Allowlisted URL Policy
recommendation.body: Implement notification tap targets only after defining the same explicit scheme/host allowlist and rejection semantics used for the broader Android URL-launch capability.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the current live assignee on this product/security-boundary issue.
